issue: C3's route-result cache (lm_route_cache, TTL + 10-min time-bucket, INVARIANT 'provider called ≤1x per (uid,event,bucket)') is fully built and unit-tested in `apps/life-call/lib/route-cache.js` but is NEVER imported or called by `travel.js`, `wake-filter.js`, or `scheduler.js`. `directionsMinutes` (travel.js:174) and its callers hit the live JP-transit/Google-Routes/legacy-Transit providers on every single invocation with zero caching, which directly defeats Goal-3 (MAPS-CACHE) — the mechanism the spec designed specifically to cap the '$100-driver' Maps Routes Compute Routes Pro cost.
evidence: grep -r 'require(.*route-cache' apps/life-call → only apps/life-call/lib/route-cache.test.js matches (zero production callers). apps/life-call/migrations/2026-07-04-lm-route-cache.sql:8-19 creates the `lm_route_cache` table but nothing writes/reads it. apps/life-call/scheduler.js:99-134 `wakeUserOnce` calls `resolveDeparture` (wake-filter.js:68-77) for EVERY shouldWake-eligible event within a 6-hour horizon on EVERY 60-second scheduler tick; `resolveDeparture` only skips the provider call when a `[Travel]` block already exists (wake-filter.js:70), which for a newly-added event can take up to 30 minutes to appear (travelTick runs every TRAVEL_TICK_MS=30min, scheduler.js:179). In that window, an uncached `directionsFn` call fires on every ~60s tick — up to ~30 paid provider calls for a single event before a cache-equivalent block exists. The builder's own evidence file admits this: `.vcsdd/features/life-manager-cost-connect-reliability/evidence/e2e-live-2026-07-03.md:8` states 'C3 (cache in live scheduler) ... require[s] the wiring + migrations (FIND-008) = the remaining phase' — i.e. the builder knows this is unwired, but this iteration is explicitly the wiring review.
fix: Call `makeRouteCache({store: supabaseLmRouteCacheAdapter, ttlMs, now}).getOrCompute(uid, fromGeo, toGeo, timeBucket(departAtMs), () => directionsMinutes(...))` from both `wake-filter.js`'s inline resolveDeparture path and `travel.js`'s fillTravel outbound/return legs, keyed per the C3 contract, before any external provider fetch. Prove the ≤1-call-per-bucket invariant with a call-count assertion against the live scheduler, not just the pure unit test.
